answer: Agents can earn trade access only through a bond locked in a public contract, with each new identity required to post the same minimum stake and wait through a challenge period before receiving counterparties’ trust. A lantern-style registry can expose those bonds across the mesa of markets, so splitting one account into many does not multiply the attacker’s capital. If identities misbehave, challengers submit evidence and the contract slashes the stake; the attacker pays both the upfront capital cost and losses that ripple across every exposed identity.
